name: Vidalytics
tagline: Hosted video player built for marketers, with engagement analytics, smart autoplay and split testing.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The interesting half of this is a player that phones home with watch events, and that is a weekend project: ffmpeg to HLS, a Video.js skin, a beacon endpoint, a retention curve chart. The boring half is video delivery, and that is where the money actually goes: transcoding ladders, adaptive bitrate, a CDN that does not stutter for a viewer in Jakarta, and mobile autoplay rules that change whenever Safari feels like it. You can rent that with S3 plus CloudFront or Bunny, which means your personal build has a hard third-party dependency and a bandwidth bill that scales with your success. The conversion features people buy this for, A/B testing thumbnails and CTAs with enough traffic to reach significance, are trivial to code and useless without volume. Build it if you host a handful of videos and mostly want your own analytics; do not build it if a sales page depends on the player loading.
coreLoopDIY: Transcodes uploaded videos to HLS, serves them through your own player page, and logs per-second watch events to a local database with a retention curve dashboard.
requirements: object storage plus a CDN, S3 with CloudFront or Bunny, credentials in .env
a small VPS or any Node host for the player page and beacon endpoint
patience for mobile autoplay and inline playback quirks
whatYouLose: Adaptive bitrate tuned by someone who does this for a living, so weak connections buffer instead of downshifting cleanly
Predictable cost: your CDN bill grows with views while a SaaS plan stays flat until a tier boundary
Split testing with built in significance math, plus the traffic reporting to know it worked
Integrations with email tools, CRMs and ad pixels that fire on watch thresholds
Someone to blame at 2am when the player breaks on a specific iOS version
moatNotes: Delivery is the product. Everything else on the marketing page is a feature list wrapped around a CDN contract.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a marketing video that stalls costs more than the subscription. People running paid traffic to a video sales letter are not shopping for an analytics hobby project, they want playback that works on every device and a number that says how many viewers made it to minute four. Vidalytics packages encoding, delivery, autoplay heuristics and conversion reporting into one bill, and the alternative is you owning a transcoding pipeline and a CDN invoice that spikes the month something goes well.
notes: The player is a weekend; the delivery is a monthly invoice either way. Decide whether you want to own the ffmpeg flags or not.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted marketing video host with engagement analytics. Empty folder, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Node 20 with TypeScript, Fastify for the server, SQLite via better-sqlite3, plain server rendered HTML with a sprinkle of vanilla JS, Video.js for playback, Chart.js for the dashboard. No React, no Next, no Docker.

In scope:
1. CLI command `npm run ingest -- ./path/to/file.mp4 --slug my-video` that uses ffmpeg to produce an HLS ladder at 1080p, 720p and 480p plus a master playlist and a poster frame, writing output to ./media/{slug}/.
2. Optional upload of ./media to S3 compatible storage using credentials from .env (S3_ENDPOINT, S3_BUCKET, S3_KEY, S3_SECRET, CDN_BASE_URL). If CDN_BASE_URL is unset, serve media straight from disk via Fastify static.
3. Public page GET /v/:slug rendering the Video.js player against the master playlist, poster, title, and an optional call to action button shown after a configurable watch percentage.
4. Embed route GET /embed/:slug returning a bare player page, plus a copyable iframe snippet in the admin UI.
5. Analytics beacon POST /api/events taking {slug, sessionId, type, position} where type is one of load, play, pause, seek, heartbeat, ended, cta_click. Client sends a heartbeat every 2 seconds while playing. Batch events with navigator.sendBeacon on pagehide.
6. Admin dashboard at /admin behind a single password from .env via basic auth: list of videos, per video plays, unique sessions, average watch time, completion rate, CTA click rate, and a retention curve computed by bucketing heartbeats into 5 second bins.
7. Config per video in a `videos` table: title, cta_text, cta_url, cta_at_percent, autoplay_muted boolean.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, multi tenancy, A/B testing, DRM, live streaming, subtitles, a mobile app, email or CRM integrations, cookie consent banners.

Rules: all secrets in .env with a committed .env.example, migrations run on boot, store no IP addresses and hash the session id, `npm run dev` must work end to end on a single machine with ffmpeg on PATH. Write a README that states the CDN bandwidth cost is now the operator's problem and shows how to point CDN_BASE_URL at a pull zone.
